stated: Labour commits to the biggest increase in social and affordable housing in a generation. They will strengthen planning obligations for more affordable homes, make changes to the Affordable Homes Programme to deliver more homes from existing funding, and support councils and housing associations to build capacity. New social rented homes will be prioritised, and existing stock better protected by reviewing increased 'right to buy' discounts and increasing protections for newly-built social housing.

source.quote: Labour will deliver the biggest increase in social and affordable housebuilding in a generation. We will strengthen planning obligations to ensure new developments provide more affordable homes; make changes to the Affordable Homes Programme to ensure that it delivers more homes from existing funding; and support councils and housing associations to build their capacity and make a greater contribution to affordable housing supply. Labour will prioritise the building of new social rented homes and better protect our existing stock by reviewing the increased right to buy discounts introduced in 2012 and increasing protections on newly-built social housing.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets social and affordable housing supply, tenure mix, right-to-buy discounts, and stock protection — all core O1 indicators (social/affordable housing stock, net additions vs need, affordability for lower incomes).

The explicit prioritisation of social rented homes (below-market housing for lower-income households) and the move to curtail right-to-buy discounts is a redistributive mechanism that concretely narrows the gap in housing costs as a share of income between lower and higher income groups, moving the Gini/income-gap indicator in a way O1 alone does not capture.

membership_note: O1 is the primary and designed-for fundamental; O14 is a genuine secondary bearing because social rent is a subsidy targeted at lower-income people, narrowing housing-cost inequality independent of aggregate supply effects. O12 is not included: the policy explicitly operates within existing Affordable Homes Programme funding, and the right-to-buy reform's net fiscal effect is too uncertain to clear the non-negligible bar. O13 (labour mobility) and O2 (general cost of living) are real but are subsumed within O1's affordability indicators and do not clear the non-negligible threshold independently.
